Article Title: ‘Came close at high speed’: What led to India-Pakistan naval collision at Arabian Sea
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Wednesday summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct” of a Pakistani naval ship. .The incident took place on the evening of September 15, when a Pakistan Naval Ship came close to a frontline Indian Navy warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea. The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in “unprofessional and unsafe manner,” sources said.No damage was reported in the incident.The MEA said the Pakistani vessel’s conduct was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991.“While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” the MEA said in a statement.The Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities that all military units must exercise due care and follow relevant agreements between the two countries.“The Charge d'Affaires of Pakistan was advised to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities, the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents,” it said.India has also instructed its Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad to lodge a similar protest with Pakistan’s ministry of foreign affairs.
Article Summary: The incident took place on the evening of September 15, when a Pakistan Naval Ship came close to a frontline Indian Navy warship. The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in “unprofessional and unsafe manner,” sources said. No damage was reported in the incident.

Article Title: India, Pakistani naval ships collide in international waters; MEA calls conduct 'unprofessional'
Article Text:
The ministry said the Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities (file photo)

What the 1991 agreement says

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct” of Pakistani naval units that led to a collision with an Indian Navy vessel in international waters.“While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” the MEA said in a statement.The ministry said the Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities that all military units must exercise due care and comply with relevant agreements between the two countries.“The Charge d'Affaires of Pakistan was advised to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities, the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents,” it said.The MEA also said India’s Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad had been instructed to lodge a similar protest with Pakistan’s ministry of foreign affairs.This is not the first time Indian and Pakistani ships have come into close contact in the Arabian Sea.In 2011, a diplomatic row had erupted over the MV Suez episode, then Navy chief Admiral Nirmal Verma said Pakistani warship PNS Babur had come “much closer” than was prudent, damaging a helicopter net on INS Godavari. He said the Indian crew had acted “very professionally” and stressed that “there are clear rules of navigation at sea”.The 1991 India-Pakistan agreement lays down rules for advance notice of major military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements.Under the agreement, the land, naval and air forces of both countries are to avoid major exercises close to each other. If such exercises are conducted within specified areas, the main force cannot be directed towards the other side and there should be no logistical build-up close to it.For land forces, exercises involving a division or larger formation are restricted within 5 km of specified areas along the International Border, Line of Control and the area between the Manawar Tawi and Ravi rivers. The agreement also requires advance notice for division-level exercises in designated areas, corps-level exercises within 75 km, and all exercises above corps level regardless of distance.For naval forces, an exercise involving six or more destroyer- or frigate-sized ships crossing into the other country's EEZ is covered. Air-force exercises at regional command level or above also fall under the agreement.
Article Summary: India summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the ‘unacceptable and unprofessional conduct’ of Pakistani naval units. The 1991 India-Pakistan agreement lays down rules for advance notice of major military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Wednesday stepped up its attack against the Centre and accused it of "giving into" United States' demand to get rid of zero MDR and charge for UPI.In a social media post on X, senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh dubbed the government's decision to introduce merchant discount rate on UPI as "NOTA - Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement" and alleged that the move was aimed at helping US card companies compete with UPI."Tomorrow, the US House of Representatives votes on a Bill that introduces 100% tariffs on India. The US Senate has already approved this draconian law. Meanwhile, the Trump regime has been cracking down on Indian immigrants and making tougher laws against them. H-1B visa costs have been increased and such holders could soon be deported immediately when out of a job. Such holders are mostly IT professionals," Jairam Ramesh said."Here, the Modi Govt has given into a US demand to get rid of zero MDR and charge for UPI. The US Trade Representative earlier this year criticized UPI for being free and having driven out Visa and Mastercard. Why 0.4% MDR? Is it because debit card MDR is also 0.4%? Is this being done to enable US card companies to compete with UPI?" he questioned.The Congress leader claimed that the estimated cost of running the entire UPI ecosystem is around Rs 20,000 crore annually, which he said is less than 10% of what the RBI has been transferring to the Union government in the past few years to show healthy public finances for the Modi government."Is this going to make UPI 'sustainable' as the Govt claims? The estimated cost of running the entire UPI ecosystem is around Rs 20,000 crore annually. Article Title: Chile, Bhutan show rabies can be beaten, but India’s 2030 target faces hurdles
Article Text:
India's huge burden of dog bites, uneven implementation of dog vaccination and population management programmes, and gaps in surveillance have been cited as key challenges in meeting its 2030 rabies elimination target. (Photo: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: While Chile and Bhutan have recently demonstrated that dog-mediated human rabies can be eliminated as a public health threat, India may struggle to meet its own 2030 elimination target, public health experts have warned. They cited the country’s huge burden of dog bites, uneven implementation of dog vaccination and population management programmes, and gaps in surveillance as key challenges.Chile recently became the first country in South America to receive World Health Organization validation for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, after more than five decades without a human case transmitted by a dog. Bhutan became the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to receive the same validation earlier this month.Both countries achieved the milestone through sustained dog vaccination, population management, surveillance, laboratory testing and access to timely post-exposure treatment, offering India a model but also highlighting the scale of effort required.The World Health Organization estimates that 9.1 million animal bites occur in India every year, with more than three-quarters caused by dogs. An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology estimate puts annual human rabies deaths at around 5,726.India’s National Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination focuses on mass dog vaccination, population management, surveillance, public awareness and timely post-exposure treatment. However, experts said the challenge lies in translating these measures into sustained action across districts.“Achieving the 2030 target will be difficult, but possible with district-level planning and coordinated action. Annual vaccination of stray dogs, effective animal birth control and dedicated spaces for strays are essential. Simply capturing them does not solve the problem,” said an expert on condition of anonymity.Dr Anil Kumar Gupta of the Association for Prevention and Control of Rabies in India and the Indian Public Health Association said the target may not be realistic at the current pace. He stressed mass dog vaccination, population management, proper wound care and timely post-exposure vaccination, while also flagging concerns over counterfeit rabies vaccines. “Never ignore a bite, even a scratch or lick,” he said.Dr Sumit Mor, Consultant & Head, Trauma & Emergency, Aakash Healthcare, said India could draw important lessons from Chile and Bhutan. “India can learn from Chile and Bhutan that rabies elimination needs sustained action, not one-off campaigns. We need dog vaccination above 70% year after year, stronger sterilisation and surveillance, mandatory case reporting, and free, uninterrupted post-exposure prophylaxis at every primary health centre.With coordinated action and sustained political commitment, the 2030 target remains within reach,” he said.The anonymous expert also pointed to competing interests around rabies control, saying a sharp fall in dog bites could affect demand for anti-rabies vaccines and rabies immunoglobulin.
Article Summary: India's huge burden of dog bites, uneven implementation of dog vaccination and population management programmes cited as key challenges. Chile recently became the first country in South America to receive World Health Organization validation for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies. An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology estimate puts annual human rabies deaths at around 5,726.

Article Title: CDSCO flags 2 Pakistani creams over excess heavy metals
Article Text:
Drug regulator alerts on unauthorised Pakistani whitening creams sale in India. (Photo: ANI)

NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has warned consumers against using two imported cosmetic creams after testing found them to be unauthorised for sale in India and containing excessive levels of heavy metals that may pose health risks.The cosmetics division of CDSCO has named Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both labelled as “Made in Pakistan”, in a public health alert dated September 8. The regulator said neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale in India.CDSCO said laboratory testing and analysis had verified that the products were unauthorised and contained heavy metals beyond specified limits, which could cause toxic effects.The regulator has advised consumers not to buy or use the two products, or similarly named products if already purchased. It has also asked sellers, distributors and other establishments not to sell, distribute or advertise them. Regulatory enforcement units have been directed to ensure that the products are not sold in their jurisdictions.CDSCO said consumers should buy only authorised cosmetics carrying details such as the manufacturing licence number, manufacturer’s details, batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, and, in the case of imported cosmetics, the registration number.The alert comes under the regulatory framework of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Cosmetics Rules, 2020. CDSCO said cosmetic manufacturing for sale requires a licence from the State Licensing Authority, while imported cosmetics must be registered with the Central Licensing Authority.
Article Summary: Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both labelled as “Made in Pakistan’, have been named in a public health alert. The regulator said neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale in India.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's public event outside London's iconic Shard skyscraper was cancelled after the Metropolitan Police raised concerns over crowd safety.Hundreds of fans had gathered at the venue, with several waiting for hours to see the actor-turned-politician. Vijay's team announced the cancellation over a loudspeaker, citing the lack of police permission on safety grounds.“For public safety concerns, we are calling off the programme because we don't have permission due to safety concerns,” a member of the chief minister's team said.Hours after the cancellation of the event, TVK's IT wing said in a social media post on X urged fans to refrain from waiting at the entrance of the hotel or making any attempts to meet him."We would be filled with love and heartfelt enthusiasm to meet the Tamil Nadu chief minister Thiru C Joseph Vijay. Therefore, with affection, we kindly request that no one attempt to meet him," TVK's IT wing said."Furthermore, with humility, we request that you refrain from efforts such as waiting at the entrance of the hotel where the victorious leader is staying or along the route he will travel," it added.Vijay is in the UK as part of a state delegation seeking investments for Tamil Nadu. His office said earlier that the delegation had signed multiple memoranda of understanding involving investments worth around Rs 12,300 crore during the visit.The investment agreements are part of the state's effort to position Tamil Nadu as a leading advanced manufacturing and technology hub in Asia. The projects are expected to create more than 9,400 high-value jobs across the state.Vijay is scheduled to conclude his UK visit and return to India on Wednesday.

Article Title: Bangladesh PM was invited for Brics meet and bilateral visit: Govt
Article Text:
Tarique Rahman

NEW DELHI: Govt reiterated Tuesday that it had invited Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman for both Brics and a bilateral visit. In a letter dated July 14, accessed by TOI, PM Narendra Modi had invited Rahman for the Brics summit in his capacity as Bimstec chair and said his participation would "greatly enrich the deliberations".After Rahman's swearing-in as PM, Modi had invited him for a bilateral visit. Dhaka, however, pulled out of talks for finalisation of the visit dates, apparently because of the lack of any firm commitment from India on ex-PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition.MEA was responding to Dhaka's claim that India had invited the Bimstec chair and not Rahman. "I have said this before as well, we had invited the PM of Bangladesh on a bilateral visit. Subsequently, he was invited for Brics summit as chair of Bimstec. So, he had received two invitations, one on the bilateral side and the other for Brics," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.Modi had also said in his letter that this year's summit was of special significance as it marked 20 years of formal establishment of Brics.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi had invited Rahman for the Brics summit in his capacity as Bimstec chair and said his participation would "greatly enrich the deliberations" After Rahman's swearing-in, Modi invited him for a bilateral visit. Article Title: Enforce speed curb device norms: SC to govts
Article Text: New Delhi: More than a decade after govt mandated installation of speed limiting devices or speed limiting functions in all public transport vehicles, enforcement remains lax, and Supreme Court Tuesday directed Centre, states and UTs to ensure compliance.Rule 118 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules provides for speed governors, and SC had passed various orders for installation of speed limiting devices. Though the SC committee on road safety had written to principal secretaries, transport secretaries and transport commissioners of all states and UTs in this regard, it was not implemented.Taking exception, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said the law had been framed by Centre and govt had to take steps to implement the statutory provision."Why does govt need directions from the court? These are statutory provisions and rules," the bench said.
Article Summary: More than a decade after govt mandated installation of speed limiting devices or speed limiting functions in all public transport vehicles, enforcement remains lax. Supreme Court Tuesday directed Centre, states and UTs to ensure compliance.Rule 118 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules provides for speed governors.

Article Title: Multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests, better centres top reform wish list
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A single bad day should not decide a student's future - and a poorly equipped examination centre should not ruin it. These concerns feature in thousands of suggestions received by the high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's examination system.The panel, led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders ahead of its next meeting, scheduled after the Brics summit. It will begin examining reform proposals, sources said.Constituted amid paper leaks, cancelled tests and infrastructure failures, the task force is examining examination security, technology, infrastructure, accessibility, student well-being and testing-agency reforms. Suggestions invited from citizens until Sept 13 will be compiled into a detailed report. A prominent demand is to give candidates multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests.Manojranjan Nayak, founder-president of Siksha 'O' Anusandhan, a deemed-to-be university, said: "Examination reform must move beyond making a flawed system more efficient. Multiple attempts can reduce the disproportionate cost of one bad day, but they should be combined with secure, accessible and uniformly equipped centres, transparent evaluation and greater weight for sustained learning.Technology can improve reliability, but it must not create a new divide between candidates with different levels of digital access. The real test of reform is whether every student, regardless of geography or income, gets a fair and dignified opportunity to demonstrate ability."Poor infrastructure at testing centres is another concern. Examinations at a Jaipur centre were disrupted by power failures on two consecutive days, affecting candidates and raising questions about how centres are selected and monitored.“For a young candidate, exam day carries years of preparation and the hopes of an entire family. If an examination is disrupted because the centre loses power or connectivity, it is not a small technical failure; it is the candidate who pays the price,” said Ashish Mittal, founder and managing director of Innovatiview.“That is why India needs Adarsh Pariksha Kendras, where reliable power, secure internet, tested computers, biometric verification and CCTV are basic standards, not last-minute arrangements. Every candidate deserves a fair examination in a centre that will not fail them,” he added.The issue is more urgent as agencies expand computer-based testing. The National Testing Agency has written to education ministry organisations seeking suitable centres. At its request, the All India Council for Technical Education has asked government technical institutions for details of computers, internet connectivity, power backup, CCTV and vacant spaces that could become standard testing centres.The government is identifying more public institutions to host entrance examinations from the next academic cycle, reducing dependence on private centres and building a more reliable national testing network.
Article Summary: High-powered task force set up to overhaul India's examination system. Panel, led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders. It is examining examination security, technology, infrastructure, accessibility, student well-being and testing agency reforms.

Article Title: Balakrishnan panel unlikely to propose inclusion of converts in SC list
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A special panel may recommend to the govt that status quo should be maintained on the definition of Scheduled Castes, as laid down by the Presidential (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, and not expanded to bring in Dalit converts to Islam and Christianity.The commission of inquiry, headed by former Chief Justice of India KG Balakrishnan, has been mandated to investigate if status of Scheduled Castes can be extended to persons who have converted to religions other than those eligible for it - popularly known as "Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam".The 1950 Presidential Order states that only persons belonging to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism can be members of Scheduled Castes.The vexed issue has been pending before Supreme Court for over 20 years in which "Dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the Scheduled Castes' list.Reports of the past commissions - Kaka Kalelkar, Sachar and Rangnath Misra - on the tricky issue, and the stand taken by National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) over the years have provided the background material for research. A 1911 book by a Christian missionary has also been relied upon.While Sachar did not recommend the Scheduled Castes status for religious converts, Misra panel did ask for the Scheduled Castes' list to be made religion-neutral. Its recommendation was apparently not accepted by govt because the panel did not conduct a study to reach its conclusion. Kalelkar commission, sources said, recommended only OBC status, and not Scheduled Castes recognition to Dalit converts.NCSC took a contradictory stand during the UPA govt, even mentioning that 50% cap on reservations should not be disturbed.According to sources, the 1911 book states that Dalits gain social status after conversion - something which seems to lighten the burden of disability which is cited for giving affirmative action benefits to Scheduled Castes. Given the inputs, the commission may recommend that the present arrangement on eligibility for inclusion in Scheduled Castes' list should stay. Besides, there is also a lack of clarity on which of the religious converts were formerly members of Scheduled Castes, sources said.Pending for over two decades, the demand of religious converts to be included in Scheduled Castes' list has become controversial because of its political dimensions. Existing Dalit communities are often found to oppose fresh inclusions in Scheduled Castes' list, arguing that such a move will increase the number of claimants for job and educational reservations.BJP argues that making Scheduled Castes status religion-neutral will encourage religious conversions.
Article Summary: The 1950 Presidential Order states that only persons belonging to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism can be members of Scheduled Castes. The vexed issue has been pending before Supreme Court for over 20 years in which "Dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the list. Existing Dalit communities often found to oppose fresh inclusions.

Article Title: Why no safety warnings for B787 fleet, US aviation group asks AAIB
Article Text:

MUMBAI: The Foundation for Aviation Safety (FAS), a US aviation safety group, has written to India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), questioning why it has not issued interim safety recommendations for the Boeing 787 fleet, despite holding evidence of chronic system failures on the aircraft involved in last year’s Ahmedabad crash, which killed 260 people.Over the past year, FAS said it had received more than 100 non-public documents specific to the crashed Air India 171 aircraft (VT-ANB). FAS sent these documents to AAIB via a UK AAIB expert.“The documents are vital to reconstructing the operational history of the doomed airplane. These documents explicitly detail chronic, systemic aircraft failures involving the airplane’s electrical, electronic, and/or flight computer systems,” said Ed Pierson, FAS executive director, in an email to AAIB director general on Aug 29. “By actively withholding this information from public announcements, the AAIB is failing its primary objective, the prevention of future accidents through timely, transparent safety manager at Boeing’s Renton 737 factory, raised internal warnings about overworked, error-prone production teams that he says went unheeded. He later founded FAS, which came into prominence for its work scrutinising Boeing’s manufacturing and safety practices in the aftermath of the 737 MAX crashes, and disclosures.Most critically, despite being in possession of evidence pointing to chronic and dangerous system failures, AAIB has issued zero interim safety recommendations or warnings to the global aviation community,” it added.Pierson, a former senior manager at Boeing’s Renton 737 factory, raised internal warnings about overworked, error-prone production teams that he says went unheeded. He later founded FAS, which came into prominence for its work scrutinising Boeing’s manufacturing and safety practices in the aftermath of the 737 MAX crashes, and has since been pressing AAIB on the AI171 investigation.In an Aug 21 letter, FAS had asked to be formally recognised as a stakeholder in the investigation and for its technical findings to be included in the investigation record. AAIB’s Aug 26 reply confirmed it received the documents via a UK AAIB expert on June 10 and that its investigation team had examined them, adding that the probe followed fair and impartial practices under the relevant regulations. AAIB did not respond to FAS’s Aug 28 letter, which alleged the agency was suppressing vital B787 safety information.AAIB told TOI, “A common update/report will be published by the AAIB.”FAS first outlined the documents’ contents in a Jan presentation to the US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. Pierson told TOI the crashed aircraft’s records showed recurring failures in its Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS).It’s the network of all wires, cables and connectors distributing electricity, data and signals through the aircraft. The 787’s EWIS spans over 150 km of wiring, more than 3,500 connectors and 40,000 cable segments. Aircraft wiring was once treated as a minor component, but after the 1996 TWA B747 and 1998 SwissAir MD-11 crashes killed a combined 529 people, EWIS emerged as a distinct, critical aircraft system on a par with engines or fuel systems. The FAA formally codified EWIS regulations in 2007.“What I do know is that VT-ANB had plenty of EWIS failures,” Pierson said, citing the non-public documents. “It also had primary power distribution failures, not just EWIS, but actual power generation, stable, high-quality electrical power. It had lots of problems with that. It had all those other issues: open circuits, short circuits, burning, arcing, fire, etc.” He said problems could arise from wiring routed too close together, chafing against sharp edges, or improper bonding and grounding, leading to electricity going places it’s not supposed to go. “You can have a lot of issues with EWIS. On landing, the P100 primary power panel was found burning, producing “12 pages of aircraft system faults”.“That’s what’s called a compound emergency... What this document shows is that the fleet is susceptible to this kind of failure, because it happened on this plane,” he said.The panel had to be replaced, a repair he compared to accessing “your circuit breaker panel at home... on steroids,” requiring technicians to cut and splice wires and reintegrate them into the system. He said the incident shows that VT-ANB itself had a history of such failures and alleged that the wider 787 fleet “is susceptible to this kind of failure”.

Article Title: DRDO has developed indigenous GaN tech for next-gen radars, electronic warfare: Def min report
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO ) has successfully demonstrated and implemented indigenous Gallium Nitride Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (GaN MMIC) Technology for high-frequency defence systems that can support next-generation radars and electronic warfare systems, the defence ministry's latest annual report for 2025-26 has revealed.After working for years, DRDO developed the GaN MMIC technology in 2024 and helped India quietly entered an elite club of seven countries — US, Russia, France, Germany, South Korea, China — after the country was reportedly denied the technology by a western nation during the negotiations for a major fighter jet deal.In layman’s language, a GaN MMIC is a tiny, super-powerful computer chip built on a special chemical material that handles extremely high-frequency wireless signals without melting. It’s an all-in-one chip that combines tiny parts—like transistors, resistors, and capacitors—onto a single piece of material to manage invisible wireless waves (microwaves).“DRDO has worked on cutting-edge defence technology and it has now matured,” a defence source told TOI. GaN is a material with exceptional thermal and electrical properties, making it critical for advanced defence applications such as sensors, radars, satellites, and missiles.“A single indigenous GaN chip, measuring 3.5 x 3 mm can deliver up to 30 watts of power and operate at speeds 300 times faster than silicon. Indigenous GaN MMIC technology for application upto X band has been successfully demonstrated and implemented,” the ministry’s report said.“Indigenously fabricated S-band GaN High Electron-Mobility power bars, power amplifier, low noise amplifier and switch MMICs have been designed, fabricated and demonstrated,” the report added.Meena Mishra, director of DRDO’s Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL) led her team that is behind the successful development of indigenous GaN MMIC technology. Over the course of more than 34 years, Meena has made significant contributions to semiconductor research and has been instrumental in the indigenous development of GaAs and GaN-based MMIC technologies for strategic applications. Her research expertise spans GaAs MESFET-based MMICs, GaAs-based digital integrated circuits, and the modeling, characterisation, and design of high-frequency devices using GaAs and GaN technologies.With rising demands for lighter and more compact power supplies in future combat systems, GaN/SiC technology provides a vital foundation for communications, intelligence, reconnaissance, and unmanned systems for both military and commercial sectors, including electric vehicles and renewable energy.
Article Summary: Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO) has successfully demonstrated and implemented indigenous Gallium Nitride Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (GaN MMIC) Technology for high-frequency defence systems. The technology can support next-generation radars and electronic warfare systems. After working for years, DRDO developed the GaNMMIC technology in 2024.

NEW DELHI: Five states and Union Territory of Delhi on Tuesday signed an agreement on the long-pending Kishau Project, which is expected to regulate water availability in the wider Yamuna basin and increase flows downstream, benefitting the national capital and Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan in one way or another. The water stored in the Kishau reservoir will augment drinking water supply for Delhi.The Kishau multi-purpose project is a proposed dam and hydropower project on the Tons river, a major tributary of the river Yamuna, flowing along the border of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Besides supplying drinking water, the multi-purpose project will also provide irrigation water for 97,000 hectares of land in riparian states and generate 1,476 million units of hydroelectric power.The agreement was signed here by all six chief ministers in the presence of Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah, who said the Centre and the chief ministers of these six states/UTs of Yamuna basin are committed to complete the project at the earliest.Calling it a “historic agreement”, Shah said Delhi will be the biggest beneficiary of the project and it will also contribute to environmental conservation by ensuring environmental flow of river Yamuna.Under the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement, an around 232-metre-high concrete gravity dam will be constructed on Tons. It will have a water storage capacity of 1,562 million cubic metres.Shah said the Centre that declared the Kishau Multipurpose Project a “national project” will bear approximately 90% of its financial burden, while the remaining 10% will be borne by the participating states in accordance with the 1994 agreement.Shah, on the occasion, recalled the signing of several other agreements on water issues and said that the period from 2018 to 2026 will be remembered as a period in which almost all water disputes, from Kashmir to Uttar Pradesh, were resolved. The foundation for these resolutions was laid in meetings of the Zonal Councils and the Ministry of Jal Shakti efficiently took these agreements forward, he added.Citing examples, Shah recalled that first, in August 2018, the dispute over the Lakhwar Multipurpose Project was resolved. In the same month, the dispute over Shahpur Kandi Dam Project was settled. In 2019, the dispute over Renukaji Multipurpose Dam Project in Upper Yamuna Basin was resolved. In 2021, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh reached an agreement on the Ken-Betwa Link Project, benefiting the water-stressed region of Bundelkhand, he added.The other projects in this league are the revised Parbati-Kalisindh-Chambal River Link project in 2024; the scheme for transferring water from Hathnikund to the Yamuna through an underground pipeline in Feb 2024; resolving dispute over the rehabilitation of families displaced by the Narmada Project in July 2026; and settling the dispute over water sharing between Bihar and Jharkhand in the river Son Basin in Aug 2026.

‘It was a political party split’

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday resumed final hearing on pleas challenging the Maharashtra Speaker’s refusal to disqualify MLAs of the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena faction, with the group defending the Election Commission ’s decision to recognise it as the “real” Shiv Sena.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana is also hearing the Uddhav Thackeray faction’s challenge to the EC’s February 17, 2023, order allotting the Shiv Sena name and ‘bow-and-arrow’ symbol to the Shinde camp.Senior advocate Neeraj Kishan Kaul, appearing for the Shinde faction, argued that the EC was empowered under Article 324 to examine a party’s constitution and organisational structure while deciding which faction represented the real party.“Your Lordships must see the entire record. The question is whether the constitution was with the Election Commission,” Kaul said.He said the constitution relied upon by the Thackeray faction was not registered with the EC, while the 1999 constitution was submitted after detailed correspondence with the poll panel.Kaul said the EC was not deciding which amendments could be made to the constitution but whether the organisational structure reflected the will of the party cadre.Rejecting the argument that the dispute was limited to a split in the legislative wing, Kaul said, “Our case has never been that there was merely a split in the legislative party. Our case is that there was a split in the political party.”He defended the EC’s organisational majority test, saying it could not conduct a referendum among every primary member of a political party.“The lifeblood of a political party is its cadre and grassroots workers who are directly connected to the electorate,” Kaul said.The hearing remained inconclusive and will continue on Wednesday.

NEW DELHI: AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi on Tuesday turned to the Constitution to counter Union home minister Amit Shah 's push to implement the Uniform Civil Code in all 21 NDA-ruled states by 2029. Hyderabad MP said that the Bhartiya Janata Party is using the proposed law to target Muslims and arguing that it could undermine key constitutional protections.Speaking to the media in Bhopal, Owaisi said the proposed law would conflict with several provisions of the Constitution.“This is against Articles 25, 26, 14 and 29 of the Constitution, and you cannot implement such a law by abolishing freedom of religion,” AIMIM leader said.His remarks came a day after he attacked Union home minister Amit Shah and the BJP over their push for the UCC.Speaking to reporters in Hyderabad on Monday, Owaisi alleged that the BJP was not seeking the UCC in the interest of equality but to target India’s Muslim population."First, you need to understand that the BJP is not pursuing the UCC for the sake of equality. Article Title: The engineers India trains, the infrastructure it still can't build
Article Text:
Too many engineers, not enough engineering

Waterlogging in Delhi

Where the engineers actually go

India's engineer surplus ends before it reaches the drains

The departments meant to absorb them are understaffed by design

What a new industrial corridor risks repeating

India's next industrial boom to happen on the East Coast

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every June, before the monsoon fully sets in, a familiar sequence plays out across Indian cities. Mumbai's suburban trains stall in ankle-deep water. Bengaluru's tech corridors flood after a single evening's rain. Delhi's underpasses fill up fast enough to trap cars. None of this is new, and none of it, by now, is unpredictable. What is harder to explain is why a country that trains more engineers than almost anywhere else on earth keeps failing at the most basic engineering problem a city faces: keeping water out and heat down.India's technical education system is producing at record scale. AICTE data shows 12.53 lakh BTech seats were filled in the 2024-25 academic session, an eight-year high and a 67 percent increase over 2017-18. But that surge is concentrated in one discipline. Computer science and engineering leads enrolment at 3,90,245 students, followed by mechanical engineering, civil engineering at 1,72,936, electronics and communication, and electrical engineering. Civil engineering, the discipline that actually builds and maintains drains, embankments and disaster-resilient housing, trails computer science by more than two to one at the point of enrolment itself, before a single graduate has even entered the job market.The surplus is real, but it isn't evenly distributed across the problems India needs solved. Computer science and IT graduates are pulled toward software, finance and consulting at a pace and pay scale that civic engineering roles, largely government postings with slower promotion cycles and lower starting salaries, cannot match. The result is a lopsided allocation: a country producing engineering talent at record volume, with that volume skewed away from the disciplines that keep cities functioning, and further skewed again once graduates choose where to build a career.This isn't a story about a shortage of trained people. It's a story about where trained people end up, and about how thin institutional capacity is on the other side of that choice, inside the departments actually responsible for stormwater drains, building safety audits and urban planning.The gap shows up starkly inside Urban Local Bodies, the municipal corporations and councils responsible for drainage, building approvals and disaster preparedness. A compendium of CAG performance audits covering 393 urban local bodies across 18 states, released in 2025, found a 42 percent gap between the revenue resources and actual expenditure of ULBs, with just 32 percent of ULB revenue self-generated and the rest arriving as grants from state and central governments. In Karnataka, government data reviewed this year showed close to 60 percent of sanctioned ULB posts vacant across ten city corporations, prompting the state to permit hiring retired engineers just to keep basic project planning functioning.Building codes compound the problem. The National Building Code, published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, is only a recommendatory document, not a binding law, so states can adopt, adapt or largely ignore its provisions. Maharashtra's own regulations don't even apply uniformly within the state: the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations explicitly exclude the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai and other planning authorities within its limits, leaving the city to run on a separate rulebook altogether.Drainage systems in most major cities were designed decades ago and were never built for the rainfall intensities cities now regularly see. On June 28, 2024, Delhi's Safdarjung Observatory recorded 228.1 mm of rainfall in 24 hours — more than three times the June average and the highest for the month in 88 years, since 1936, according to the India Meteorological Department. The waterlogging and traffic disruption that followed looked no different from floods a decade earlier.This matters beyond the annual monsoon cycle because India is now committing serious capital to exactly the kind of large-scale infrastructure build-out that depends on this workforce functioning well. The East Coast Industrial Corridor, pegged to the Union Budget 2026-27's announcement of a Durgapur-anchored industrial belt spanning ports, manufacturing zones and logistics networks across Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, is one of several major infrastructure pushes riding on the assumption that India's technical capacity can execute at scale. But the same staffing vacancies, advisory-only codes and enforcement gaps that produce annual urban flooding sit underneath these new projects too. A corridor is, in the end, drainage, ports, road networks and disaster-resilient construction multiplied across four states; the same civic engineering functions currently understaffed in every city that already exists.The heat side of the problem makes the stakes clearer still. India's peak power demand climbed from 214.9 GW on April 1 to a record 270.8 GW on May 21, 2026, according to the Union Ministry of Power, a 26 percent jump in fifty days, driven by sustained heat. That's a building-design and urban-planning failure as much as a climate one: cool roofs, passive ventilation and heat-resilient construction are still treated as add-ons rather than baseline requirements in most bye-laws.A multi-city study analysing roughly 3.6 million deaths across ten Indian cities between 2008 and 2019 found that heatwave days were associated with a 14.7 percent increase in daily mortality, and estimated around 1,116 deaths a year attributable to heatwaves. The 2025 Report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change estimated that India lost about 247 billion labour hours to heat exposure in 2024, translating to roughly $194 billion in economic losses, concentrated in agriculture and construction.None of this points to a talent problem. India has the engineers, more of them, and more concentrated in one discipline, than ever before. What it doesn't have, consistently, is a civic system built to employ the rest where the predictable failures actually happen, inside municipal drainage departments, building-approval desks and disaster-management cells that are short-staffed and underfunded by a documented, audited margin.Every large infrastructure announcement adds new physical assets to maintain. Unless the capacity gap inside the institutions responsible for maintaining them closes at the same pace, each new corridor, each new industrial belt, inherits the same vulnerability the rest of urban India already lives with every monsoon and every summer.
Article Summary: India's technical education system is producing at record scale. AICTE data shows 12.53 lakh BTech seats were filled in the 2024-25 academic session. Computer science and engineering leads enrolment at 3,90,245 students. Civil engineering trails computer science by more than two to one at the point of enrolment.

Article Title: ‘He had received two invitations’: India rejects confusion over Bangladesh PM’s Brics invite
Article Text:
Tarique Rahman received separate India invites for bilateral visit and Brics, MEA says

Brics invitation came as Bimstec chair

Bilateral visit invitation also remains in place

NEW DELHI: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had received two separate invitations from India — one for a bilateral visit and another to attend the Brics Summit as chair of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (Bimstec), the ministry of external affairs said on Tuesday.Addressing the MEA’s weekly press briefing, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal clarified the nature of the invitations amid questions over whether Rahman had been invited to the Brics Summit in New Delhi.“We had invited the Prime Minister of Bangladesh on a bilateral visit, and subsequently, he was invited for the Brics Summit as chair of Bimstec. So, he had received two invitations, one on the bilateral side and the other for the Brics Summit as well,” Jaiswal said.Bangladesh is neither a Brics member nor a partner country. India had invited Rahman to the outreach session of the 18th Brics Summit in his capacity as the current chair of Bimstec, according to an earlier MEA briefing.The Brics Summit was held in New Delhi from September 12 to 13, bringing together leaders of member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees.The clarification from the MEA came after Bangladeshi officials had said Rahman was not invited to the summit in his capacity as Bangladesh’s prime minister.Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir had said last week that the invitation was extended to the Bimstec chair rather than to Rahman as Bangladesh’s prime minister.“How shall we go? Has anyone from the Bangladesh government been invited? Our PM was not invited. Who told you that our PM was invited? The Bimstec Chair was invited. Then why are you asking this question?” Kabir had told reporters.Jaiswal’s remarks also reiterated that India had separately invited Rahman for a bilateral visit.The bilateral invitation had been extended in February. India had sent Lok Sabha Speaker Om Prakash Birla to attend the inauguration of Rahman’s BNP government on February 17 following Bangladesh’s February 12 general elections.Birla had carried a letter from Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulating Rahman and inviting him to India along with his wife and daughter.Kabir had earlier said Bangladesh was placing greater emphasis on arranging a bilateral visit for Rahman and that his first visit to India should not be a multilateral one. He had said the government was working to arrange the bilateral visit when the timing was conducive.The issue comes against the backdrop of strained India-Bangladesh ties over several unresolved matters, including former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India, extradition requests and water-sharing issues, while Dhaka has also been strengthening its engagement with China and Pakistan.
Article Summary: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman received separate India invites for bilateral visit and Brics, MEA says. India invited Rahman to the outreach session of the 18th Brics Summit in his capacity as the current chair of Bimstec. Bangladesh is neither a Brics member nor a partner country.

Article Title: ‘Such gimmicks are nothing new’: India slams Pakistan over 'phoney announcement' of Rs 70 lakh bounty on Masood Azhar
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday criticised Pakistan over its announcement of a PKR 70 lakh reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar , calling it a “phoney” move and asking Islamabad to take concrete action against the terror group chief.Responding to Pakistan maintaining the bounty on Azhar, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Islamabad's announcement was unlikely to have any consequence."Such gimmicks and attempts at hoodwinking people by Pakistan are nothing new. We have seen similar gimmicks in the past as well. For a state sponsor of terrorism to make such phoney announcements—we all know how hollow they are. Pakistan must take concrete action rather than make announcements that are ultimately of no consequence..."Pakistan has continued to list Azhar in the Federal Investigation Agency's (FIA) “Red Book” of most-wanted terrorists and has retained a reward of PKR 70 Lakh for information leading to his apprehension or conviction.Also read | Pakistan lists Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar as fugitive, hikes bounty ahead of FATF review Azhar, the founder and chief of JeM, is wanted in India in connection with several terror cases, including the 2001 Parliament attack. India has also linked JeM to the 2016 Pathankot airbase attack and the 2019 Pulwama bombing.His name was first included in the FIA's Red Book in 2021 and has been retained in its 2026 edition. He is listed at serial number 1480 among 1,804 most-wanted terrorists.The FIA entry identifies Azhar as the head of Jaish-e-Mohammad and says the reward of up to PKR 70 lakh is for information leading directly to his “apprehension or conviction”.The cases cited against him in the FIA list were registered in Gujranwala, Multan and Lahore under provisions of Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act.India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar. Islamabad has maintained that he fled to Afghanistan, a claim rejected by Afghanistan's Taliban government.Azhar was among the fugitives India sought from Pakistan following the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, in which 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists killed 166 people.The latest development comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force's next plenary in Paris from October 26 to 30. Pakistan was placed on the FATF's increased monitoring list, commonly known as the grey list, in 2018 and remained there until 2022.It was removed after completing commitments under two FATF action plans focused on strengthening its anti-money laundering and counter-terror financing framework and implementing targeted financial sanctions.
Article Summary: Pakistan has retained a reward of PKR 70 Lakh for information leading to his apprehension or conviction. Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar is wanted in India in connection with several terror cases. India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar.

Article Title: ‘No child should be deprived of dignity’: Delhi HC allows 15-year-old rape survivor to terminate pregnancy
Article Text:
Delhi HC allows termination of pregnancy of rape survivor

'15-year-old cannot be reduced to description of mother'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has held that compelling a rape survivor to continue with a pregnancy resulting from sexual assault and forcing motherhood upon her against her will would seriously impair her right to live with dignity.The court made the observation while allowing a plea filed on behalf of a 15-year-old rape survivor seeking termination of her pregnancy, which had crossed 30 weeks of gestation, news agency PTI reported.Justice Madhu Jain said the fact that the pregnancy had crossed the statutory limit under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act could not, by itself, be considered in isolation in cases arising from sexual assault.Justice Jain said courts exercising jurisdiction under Articles 226 or 32 of the Constitution must give due primacy to the best interests and welfare of the minor, while also taking into account the statutory framework under the MTP Act.The court described the case as "unfortunate and distressing", noting that the girl was only 15, had already suffered the trauma of an alleged heinous sexual assault and had lost both her parents."A child of 15 years cannot, in the eyes of this court, be reduced to the description of a 'mother' merely because she has been forced into pregnancy as a consequence of sexual violence," it said.The court said that while the law could provide remedies and procedures, no judicial order could undo the trauma the child had endured.Allowing the plea, the court directed the medical superintendent of Lady Hardinge Medical College and S K Hospital to arrange for termination of the pregnancy at the earliest and maintain a record of the procedure.The doctors were also directed to preserve the tissue or foetal material for DNA identification and other purposes in connection with the criminal case registered over the rape.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court allows termination of pregnancy of rape survivor. '15-year-old cannot be reduced to description of mother' says court. Doctors directed to preserve tissue or foetal material for DNA identification and other purposes in connection with the criminal case.

As Bengaluru continues to expand towards its emerging growth corridors, homebuyers are increasingly looking beyond just location and square footage. Privacy, open spaces, sustainability and everyday liveability are becoming equally important considerations. Urbanest Realty’s Eastfield, located off OMR in Hoskote, has been designed around these priorities.Spread across 2.75 acres, Eastfield comprises twin residential towers with 200 premium 3-BHK homes. One of the project’s defining features is its low-density planning. Only 9% of the land is used for tower construction, leaving 91% as open space for landscaped areas, recreation and lifestyle amenities.Privacy has also been central to the project’s design. With only four families per floor, all homes are positioned as corner residences with no common walls. The orientation of the twin towers has been planned to allow natural daylight and cross-ventilation across the residences, while offering 180-degree panoramic views from the homes.Connectivity is another important aspect of Eastfield’s positioning. The project is connected to key infrastructure corridors, including the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway, and is located around 900 metres from the Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR). It is also within walking distance of the proposed upcoming Hoskote Metro station, adding to its long-term connectivity potential.The development offers 40-plus lifestyle amenities across its open spaces and clubhouse areas. These include three swimming pools, with one exclusively for women inside the clubhouse, water fountains, seating areas, an outdoor party lawn, pet park, indoor and outdoor gyms, and several community-focused spaces.For sports and outdoor recreation, Eastfield has a dedicated 2-plus-acre multi-sport arena featuring a dribble court, tennis and basketball courts, cricket pitch, cycling track and jogging track, along with social and community zones.Sustainability and urban resilience also form part of the planning. Eastfield includes an advanced rainwater harvesting and water-storage system designed to support drinking-water requirements for up to 100 days. Solar panels for common-area lighting and EV-charging infrastructure further contribute to the project’s future-ready approach.Another notable feature of the project is a 15,000 sq ft clubhouse serving 200 residences, a rare combination. It has been planned as a comprehensive lifestyle space with a fully functional gym, yoga and meditation room, unisex salon, indoor multipurpose hall and event lawn for celebrations, gatherings and community activities.Urbanest Realty describes its approach as combining modern design, practical planning and a customer-first mindset, with homes designed around both everyday comfort and long-term value.The developer and Eastfield have also received industry recognition in recent years. In 2025, Urbanest Realty was named Emerging Developer of the Year – South India at both the India Property Awards and the Economic Times Business Awards, while Eastfield received Residential Project of the Year at the Economic Times Business Awards 2025.In 2026, Eastfield was named Luxury Apartment Project of the Year at the Southern Achievers Awards – Outlook Business Spotlight, while Urbanest Realty was recognised for Excellence in Premium Lifestyle Plotted Venture at the Times Real Estate Awards.At Eastfield, 3-BHK residences range from 1,744 sq ft to 1,886 sq ft, with prices starting from approximately ₹1.6 crore onwards, bringing together low-density planning, privacy, connectivity, lifestyle amenities and sustainable infrastructure within one residential development.

Article Title: 'Once again surrendering to US pressure': Rahul slams govt over UPI fee exemption limit
Article Text:
UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 to remain free of charge.

What does the notification say?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul on Tuesday accused the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government of “surrendering to pressure from American corporations” by reportedly paving the way for charges on certain Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions.Rahul argued that although the government has said consumers will not be charged directly, allowing a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 could eventually lead to higher retail prices.Sharing a post on X, the leader of opposition said, "The Modi government has quietly opened the door to imposing fees on UPI. Now, MDR can be levied on merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. Even if these transactions account for just 5% of the volume, they make up nearly 65% of UPI's total transaction value.""The government says no fees will be charged to customers. But where will the fees imposed on shopkeepers ultimately come from? Added to prices, straight out of the customer's pocket. American payment companies have long opposed India's zero-MDR policy. Now, the Modi government has opened the path to changing the policy in exactly that direction. Just like with the US Trade Deal, Compromised PM Modi is once again surrendering to American pressure," he added.Rahul’s remarks came after the government directed banks and payment system providersnot to impose direct or indirect charges on UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000or on payments made through RuPay debit cards.However, the notification does not clarify whether charges could be imposed on transactions above Rs 2,000, particularly those made by merchants. UPI transactions have so far remained free of charges, irrespective of the amount.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also accused the PM Modi government of laying the groundwork for a “Digital Payments Tax” by allowing the possibility of charges on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.“The Modi government's loot has now reached UPI. "No fees on UPI" has been changed to "no fees on UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000." Sky-high inflation has already emptied the common man's pocket. Wholesale inflation is near 10%, and the BJP government has planned to impose a "Digital Payments Tax" on the public, aiming to destroy whatever little savings they have left,” Kharge said in an X post.“Ten years ago, demonetization delivered a shock to the country's economy. When questions were raised about the disastrous outcomes of demonetization, the government argued that it was imposed to promote Digital Payments and a Cashless Economy. The Finance Minister had recently stated in Parliament that no Tax or Charges would be levied on UPI, but according to several reports: A potential collection of Rs 25 on a Rs 5,000 transaction and up to Rs 50 on Rs 10,000. Is this true?” he added.He also warned that any Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) imposed on merchants could eventually be passed on to consumers through higher prices.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh also questioned whether the transaction limit could be changed through a future notification to cover person-to-person transfers.“It is evident that the groundwork is being laid to collect fees on UPI transactions from all of us. Tomorrow, through another similar notification, this limit could also be altered—there is now no guarantee of this in the law. As far as we know, the government could impose charges even on everyday person-to-person UPI transactions,” he wrote on X. “Is all this being done with the intent of opening up digital payments for American companies to please President Trump?” he asked.According to a gazette notification dated September 14, no bank or system provider can impose a direct or indirect charge on a person making or receiving a payment through a RuPay debit card or a UPI transaction of up to Rs 2,000.The notification follows an amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The amendment provides an enabling framework for imposing MDR on UPI and other notified electronic payment modes.The amendment Bill was passed by Parliament during the Monsoon Session, which concluded on August 13, 2026. The government had said that the UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), would decide the MDR rates.The government has argued that rising transaction volumes require continuous investment in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and payment infrastructure. It has also said that charges would support market expansion, encourage competition and help create a self-sustaining revenue model for the payments ecosystem.UPI is operated by NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India and the Indian Banks’ Association. It enables real-time payments between individuals and allows customers to pay merchants directly.Launched on August 25, 2016, UPI has transformed India’s digital payments landscape. Its transaction value rose from Rs 0.07 lakh crore in FY17 to around Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26, an increase of more than 4,000 times in a decade.UPI is now accepted in 11 countries, including Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Greece and Uzbekistan.According to Reuters, the introduction of UPI charges could benefit Paytm and Pine Labs, create an additional revenue stream for banks and improve prospects for IPO-bound PhonePe and Razorpay. Analysts at Jefferies estimate that the fees could generate Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 10,000 crore annually for the payments industry.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul accused the PM Modi-led government of “surrendering to pressure from American corporations’ Rahul’s remarks came after the government directed banks and payment system providersnot to impose direct or indirect charges on UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000.

Article Title: Stock market holiday: Are NSE, BSE closed for trading on Ganesh Chaturthi?
Article Text:
Stock market holiday on September 14

What happens to trading and settlement?

What about commodity markets?

Upcoming stock market holidays in 2026

Date Day Holiday September 14, 2026 Monday Ganesh Chaturthi October 2, 2026 Friday Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti October 20, 2026 Tuesday Dussehra November 10, 2026 Tuesday Diwali-Balipratipada November 24, 2026 Tuesday Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev December 25, 2026 Friday Christmas

Ganesh Chaturthi is falling on Monday, September 14 and investors are wondering whether the festival will affect trading in the stock and commodity markets.NSE and BSE follow their own trading holiday calendars, which are separate from holidays observed by banks and government offices. According to the 2026 exchange calendar, both NSE and BSE will remain closed for trading on September 14 on account of Ganesh Chaturthi. Investors will therefore not be able to buy or sell shares on either exchange during the regular trading session on Monday. Equity derivatives trading will also remain closed.The commodity market, however, follows a different schedule. Article Title: Roger Federer built an $8.1 million glass mansion on Lake Zurich; after listing his Wollerau villa for $5.3 million, he sold it as plans grew for a massive new waterfront compound
Article Text:
Roger Federer built an $8.1 million glass mansion on Lake Zurich; after listing his Wollerau villa for $5.3 million, he sold it as plans grew for a massive new waterfront compound

What did Roger Federer’s $8.1 million Wollerau glass mansion include

Why did Roger Federer put his Wollerau villa up for sale

How did Roger Federer’s Rapperswil-Jona property change his plans

What is planned for Roger Federer’s new Lake Zurich estate

Where does Roger Federer’s Swiss and global property portfolio stand

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Roger Federer’s former Wollerau home near Lake Zurich was one of his most striking properties, but the Swiss tennis great eventually put the glass residence on the market as his plans changed. The three-story home, known as “The Residence,” covered about 500 square metres and included large glass walls, balconies, a pool and underground parking. Federer reportedly listed the property for 5.4 million Swiss francs, about $5.3 million, in 2017. It was sold the following year. By then, Federer had already moved his Swiss base to Valbella and was looking toward a much larger waterfront project in Rapperswil-Jona.Federer’s Wollerau home stood in the canton of Schwyz, on the shores of Lake Zurich. He had the modern property built as a family home, with the project completed around 2014. Architectural Digest India reported that the house was worth about £6.5 million at the time and had three levels with around 500 square metres of space.The design was built around the lake view. Floor-to-ceiling glass brought in plenty of natural light, while large balconies looked out toward the water.The property also had a swimming pool and underground parking.The home was not only for Federer, his wife Mirka and their four children. A separate living space was also planned for his parents, Robert and Lynette. That made the property more than a luxury house for the tennis star; it was designed to keep his wider family close while giving everyone their own space.Federer’s plans for Wollerau changed over time. He had already moved his official residence to Valbella in the Swiss canton of Graubünden in 2015. In 2017, the Wollerau property was put up for sale, with the asking price reported at 5.4 million Swiss francs.The exact final sale price was not publicly confirmed. Local reports said the property was eventually bought by a wealthy person from the canton of Zurich, who worked in the wealth-management sector. The sale was reported in July 2018.That detail matters because the $5.3 million figure refers to the reported asking price or estimated value, not a confirmed final transaction price. The Bote der Urschweiz reported that the actual amount paid was not known, although it was believed to be around that level.While Federer was leaving Wollerau, another Lake Zurich project was taking shape. In 2018, he acquired a large waterfront property in Kempraten, part of Rapperswil-Jona. The site covers roughly 16,000 to 18,000 square metres, depending on how the property area has been reported. Swiss reports placed the land’s value at around 40 million to 50 million Swiss francs.The new project was far larger than the Wollerau home. Plans included several buildings, a tennis court and sports facilities, with the property giving the Federer family direct access to Lake Zurich.The project has not moved as quickly as originally expected. Construction has faced objections and disputes linked to the waterfront, environmental issues and access along the lake. Swiss public broadcaster SRF reported in 2019 that the building permit had been approved, while later reports showed that the project continued to face delays.By August 2025, Swissinfo reported that construction was moving ahead. The site was then described as almost 17,000 square metres, with several buildings under development. The report also said that the family had originally hoped to move there in 2021.The Rapperswil-Jona property is meant to give Federer and his family much more room than the old Wollerau residence. Reports have described a group of buildings rather than one single villa, along with a tennis court and indoor sports facilities.Le Temps reported in 2024 that the property covered more than 16,000 square metres and that Federer was building about half a dozen structures there. The report estimated the land purchase at around 50 million Swiss francs, with another 20 million francs expected in construction costs.There is also a planned boat facility, although that part of the project has faced a separate dispute. The Swiss federal authorities challenged approval for the boat shelter, according to Le Temps.The scale of the project shows why the Wollerau house no longer fit Federer’s plans. Instead of one three-story residence on a relatively small plot, the new property gives his family a much larger private space on the lake.Federer still has strong links to several parts of Switzerland. His Valbella properties in the Lenzerheide area have been part of his Swiss real estate holdings, while his Rapperswil-Jona project has become his biggest known residential development.He also owns property in Dubai. Architectural Digest reported that Federer has a luxury penthouse in the Le Reve tower in Dubai Marina, with the property estimated at about $23.5 million.Federer has also sold other Swiss property over the years. In 2024, Blick reported that he sold a roughly 5,800-square-metre plot in Herrliberg, another location on Lake Zurich.That makes the Wollerau sale part of a wider change in Roger Federer’s property holdings. The glass home was built as a high-end family residence during his playing career, but within a few years he had sold it and shifted his attention to a much bigger waterfront project in Rapperswil-Jona.
Article Summary: Roger Federer built an $8.1 million glass mansion on Lake Zurich. After listing his Wollerau villa for $5.3 million, he sold it as plans grew for a massive new waterfront compound. The three-story home covered about 500 square metres and included large glass walls, balconies, a pool and underground parking.

Article Title: Govt to build hostels for 10,000 students, says Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi government will construct ten thousand student hostels for safe accommodation.





NEW DELHI: Days after the Satya Niketan tragedy, chief minister Rekha Gupta Tuesday announced that Delhi govt would construct hostels for 10,000 students to “provide them a safe, supportive place to stay, so they can study with peace of mind and move closer to the future they came here to build”.“Lakhs of students come to Delhi for study; they get admission but not hostels... (They) will be provided safe and economic accommodation. These hostels will be made for girls as well as boys from any university,” Gupta said, adding that hostels are required for making Delhi a big education hub. The scope of the initiative will be expanded as per the growing need, chief minister’s office said.On Sept 6, a five-storey building being used as a paying guest facility for students collapsed in Satya Niketan near Delhi University’s South Campus, killing seven people, including five DU students. The incident brought back into focus the issue of lack of safe and adequate accommodation facilities for students and triggered demands for institutional housing facilities.The construction is already under way or has been proposed at several institutions, including Ambedkar University, Dhirpur, GB Pant Engineering College and Polytechnic, Indira Gandhi Hospital and Medical College, and Delhi Sports University.Various departments, such as health, higher education, and women and child development, are getting the hostels constructed under the public-private partnership model. Govt will also conduct a survey of colleges that have sufficient space for hostel construction.An official said hostels would have essential facilities, including Wi-Fi, 24-hour electricity and water supply, study rooms, libraries and hygienic messes. Round-the-clock security will be ensured through CCTV surveillance and biometric entry systems. Fire safety measures and regular structural audits will be accorded the highest priority to ensure a safe and secure living environment for students, the official said.“We will make such hostels where parents from different parts of the country can leave their children without worry. The students also need not worry about food and accommodation, rather they can concentrate on their dreams,” said CM.Delhi faces a severe shortage of institutional hostel accommodation. DU, for instance, has around 2.5 lakh regular students, many of whom come from outside the city, but currently has hostel capacity for only 7,210, forcing a large number of students to live in unsafe and uncomfortable PG accommodations at high rents. Many of these buildings have been constructed in densely populated areas in violation of building norms. DU has planned to expand the capacity to 12,754 seats, still falling short of the requirement.Soon after the Satya Niketan incident, a high-level meeting, chaired by lieutenant governor TS Sandhu and attended by CM, was held to examine the issue. Education minister Ashish Sood recently promised a student delegation that govt would introduce comprehensive legislation and regulations for paying guest accommodations within two months. The policy, being drafted by an 18-member high-level committee, is likely to introduce mandatory licences for PGs, zone-wise rent bands, structural and fire-safety audits, and a central portal listing rents, amenities and compliance details.
Article Summary: Chief minister Rekha Gupta announced that Delhi govt would construct hostels for 10,000 students. Hostels will be made for girls as well as boys from any university. The scope of the initiative will be expanded as per the growing need, chief minister’s office said.
